description: A user understands that their policy contains coverage rules and exclusions, but they need help interpreting what those terms actually mean for three specific real-life situations they worry about.

user_profile.persona: 31-year-old freelance photographer buying more serious coverage for the first time
user_profile.context: The policy wording feels abstract until connected to actual situations involving work equipment and travel
user_profile.communication_style: Concrete and example-driven, learns best through scenario-based explanation

fact_sheet.fact: The policyholder is Liam Chen, a 31-year-old freelance photographer.
Liam Chen holds the 'ProLens Secure Plan' with Aegis Mutual Insurance.
The policy number is PLS-884-391-C2, with an effective date of March 1, 2024.
The annual premium for the ProLens Secure Plan is $1,250.
The policy includes 'Specialized Equipment Coverage' with a total limit of $20,000.
Liam's Sony Alpha 1 camera body (Serial: SN-A1-98765) is a scheduled item on the policy with a replacement value of $6,500.
A $500 deductible applies to each claim for accidental damage to photography equipment.
The policy covers accidental damage, such as dropping a G Master 70-200mm lens on a rock during a shoot, but excludes cosmetic wear and tear.
Damage to drones, like Liam's DJI Mavic 3 Pro, is only covered if it occurs within 500 feet of the operator and not over water.
The policy includes 'Business Trip Interruption' coverage, which reimburses up to $5,000 in non-refundable, pre-paid travel costs.
A covered reason for trip interruption is the cancellation of transportation due to a natural disaster, such as a wildfire near a photoshoot location.
Liam's non-refundable $485 ticket for Skyward Air flight SW451 would be eligible for reimbursement if the flight is canceled due to a wildfire.
The 'Business Trip Interruption' coverage does not reimburse for lost potential income from the canceled photoshoot.
The policy provides 'General Liability Coverage' with a limit of $1,000,000 per occurrence.
The liability coverage applies if a third party, such as a model or client, is injured as a direct result of Liam's professional operations.
If a model named Alex Rivera tripped over a tripod leg and sprained an ankle, the policy's liability coverage would handle the claim.
The policy includes a 'Medical Payments' sub-limit of $10,000 to cover immediate medical expenses for an injured third party, regardless of fault.
There is a $0 deductible for claims filed under the General Liability portion of the policy.
Liam must report any incident that could lead to a liability claim to Aegis Mutual Insurance within 72 hours of its occurrence.
To file a claim, Liam must use the Aegis Mutual online portal located at https://my.aegismutual.net/claims.
For an equipment damage claim, Liam needs to provide the item's serial number and a repair estimate from a certified technician.
For a trip interruption claim, Liam must submit the flight cancellation email from the airline and proof of pre-payment.
The average processing time for a fully documented equipment claim is 7-10 business days.
Liam's dedicated insurance agent is Sarah Jenkins, reachable at s.jenkins@aegismutual.net or 800-555-0182 ext. 445.
The policy territory for all coverages is the United States and Canada; international shoots require a separate rider.
